title: Weaver checks
description: What the project's own programs check, each with the rules it stands behind. A check judges the diff of a unit of work at the end of a task; it may repair before it judges, and warn right after a tool call. Each key is the name of a check.

$schema.description: The schema this file follows, for the editor.

warn.description: A command that warns the agent early, right after one of its tool calls changed files the check is about: a fast run on those files alone, where an argument `{files}` becomes them. What it finds is told to the agent with the result of the call and holds nothing: `judge` gives the verdict. Its result is read as `reads` says, and its time is `checks.warnTimeoutSeconds` in `settings.json`.

repair.description: A command that repairs what it can before `judge` judges what is left: a formatter, a linter's autofix, a generator. It runs on the unit's own files, and what it rewrites stays the agent's work.

judge.description: The command that judges, with its arguments, when the agent says it has finished. An argument `{files}` becomes the changed files the check is about.

cwd.description: Where the command runs, relative to the repository root.

when.description: The changed paths that make the check run, as globs. Without it, any change does.

reads.description: How the verdict of `judge`, and what `warn` found, is read. `exit`: from the exit status. `findings`: from the last line printed, `{"findings": [...]}`, where each finding gives the name of a `rule`, a `file`, a `message` and optionally a `line`.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one run of `judge` or of `repair` may take.

after.description: The check that must be done before this one starts, for a check that reads another's output.

rules.description: The rules this check stands behind. Each key is the name of a rule, as the agent and the owner read it: `no-any` says more than a code. A check with no rule of its own lists places for a rule of `llm/rules.json` that names it as its `candidates`.

checkRule.description: A rule a check stands behind. Its sentence alone is a rule for the agent, which is held until it is fixed. An object says who a failure is for.

statement.description: What the rule says, as it is told to whoever broke it.

level.description: Who a failure is for. `gate`: the agent, which is held until it is fixed. `human`: the owner, who reads it in the report; the agent is not held.
